## `Verified -1` on patchset 1 root-caused: not a defect in this change

Re-derived from the live run rather than from notes. Run
[35510440501](https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/35510440501) against patchset 1
(rev `f2200580a17`) failed in exactly one matrix cell — `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.11)` —
with exactly one test:

    FAILED tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py::test_worker_cancellation_survives_job_completion_race
      - worker 'gw3' crashed while running [...]

    1 failed, 20443 passed, 80 skipped, 29 warnings in 1076.81s

That test is untouched by this change, which streams Jira DC harness test progress. The
crash is the opcert teardown join hanging until xdist kills the worker — bug
`68a9-2a6c-d9aa-49ad`, fixed by change 3009, merged at 14:46:33Z as `641531e62e5`.

## Why a rebase, not a `recheck`

`recheck` would not have helped, and this is worth recording because the instinct is wrong
here. `gerrit-verify.yaml` checks out **the exact patchset** via
`checkout-gerrit-change-action` (`_build-and-test.yml:57`); there is no rebase-onto-target
step. Patchset 1's parent was `e84e4c5e943`, which predates both `e50e733aaa3` and the fix
at `641531e62e5`, so a re-run would have tested the same wedged tree and failed identically.

The fix has to be *in this change's own history* for CI to go green, so patchset 2 is a
clean rebase onto `641531e62e5`. `Change-Id`, `rebar-ticket:` trailer and sign-off all
carried forward; no content change — `git rebase` reported no conflicts and the diff is
unchanged.

This also is not a retry of a flaky test. The flake was root-caused, fixed, reviewed and
merged as its own change; rebasing onto that fix is picking up the remedy, not re-rolling
the dice.

## Patchset 2 is red on an unrelated test-scaffolding defect, not on this change

`Verified -1` on patchset 2 (`db06c1257a9`), GitHub Actions run
[35517603759](https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/35517603759). The py3.11 crash
that sank patchset 1 is **gone** — that was `68a9`'s opcert teardown race, and rebasing onto
the merged fix (`641531e62e5`) cleared it, which is the differential confirming `68a9`'s fix
works in CI.

The new failure is a different one, in the gating py3.13 cell:

```
tests/unit/test_pinned_ticket_view.py::test_tree_listed_ticket_blob_missing_from_object_database_fails_closed[packed-_drop_packed]
E  AssertionError: expected fb9d1b4935c7f78e7d91558bed4bd8445b88da3a to be loose
1 failed, 20479 passed, 82 skipped
```

This change streams Jira DC harness test progress and touches nothing on the pinned-view or
ticket-store path, so it is not the cause. Root-caused and filed as `4a6f-0fd8-a04a-4e95`
(`dollish-puzzled-pupfish`): the packed parametrization's setup helper reuses `_drop_loose`,
which asserts the blob is stored as a LOOSE object — so the route that exists to cover the
already-packed shape fails on exactly that shape.

**Not rechecking.** A flaky test is a bug to root-cause, and CI checks out the exact patchset
with no rebase step, so a recheck would re-test this same code against the same defect. This
change unblocks when `4a6f` lands and this change is rebased onto it.

## Closing evidence — AC10 satisfied by a dispatched post-merge run

AC10 was the last open criterion and is marked `[non-codebase]` because its
evidence is a live GitHub Actions run against real Jira Data Center, not
anything readable from the tree.

### The run

`external-integration.yml` (registered as **Live External Integration**,
workflow id `296028316`) was dispatched against `main` after this ticket's fix
merged. No qualifying completed post-merge run existed beforehand — the latest
completed dispatch was `35508005436` at `e84e4c5e`, which does not contain the
merge `254d076cb50ef01bcded5e35bba09e1b6f240cc2`, so a fresh dispatch was
required rather than reusing an older run.

**Run `35534905486`**, head `ba878272701217b42fac59e4241e69eab24097fe`, event
`workflow_dispatch`.
https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/35534905486

Job `jira DC harness smoke (real Jira Data Center, ephemeral)`, step
`Run the Jira DC harness smoke tests`, ran `2026-09-20T20:19:41Z` →
`2026-09-20T22:29:42Z`.

### The measurement

The defect was that the entire ~2-hour pytest step collapsed onto a single log
timestamp, so a healthy long run and a hung one were indistinguishable from the
outside. The post-merge step emits **238 distinct timestamps across 239 log
lines** — effectively one timestamp per line, which is the opposite of the
reported behaviour.

Progress is now visible as it happens:

```
2026-09-20T20:27:40.5782319Z tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_mutation_round_trips[02-edit-summary] PASSED [  1%]
2026-09-20T20:30:12.1918906Z tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_mutation_round_trips[03-edit-description] PASSED [  2%]
2026-09-20T20:32:47.0609990Z tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_mutation_round_trips[04-transition-status] PASSED [  3%]
2026-09-20T20:35:20.1928779Z tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_mutation_round_trips[05-add-label] PASSED [  5%]
2026-09-20T20:37:55.2142579Z tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_mutation_round_trips[06-remove-label] PASSED [  6%]
```

Roughly two and a half minutes separate consecutive tests, each stamped as it
completes. An observer can now tell a progressing run from a stalled one.

### On the run's overall conclusion

The workflow's conclusion was `failure`, and that does **not** weaken this
evidence. `Live External Integration` is an advisory/manual lane against real
Jira Data Center — it is not in the Gerrit `Verified` hot path, and the
`Verified +1` this change already carries came from the gating matrix. The
criterion asks whether the pytest step emits more than one distinct timestamp,
and the step emitted 238 regardless of how its assertions landed. A failing
assertion inside a step whose log is now legible is precisely the situation
this ticket existed to make possible.

The remaining failure in that lane is external-integration behaviour against
live Jira DC and is not this ticket's subject; it is out of scope here rather
than silently absorbed.

## Problem

The `jira-dc-harness` job's pytest step emitted no useful progress for its ~2-hour runtime, then flushed the log at the end. A healthy live-Jira run therefore looked like a hang, and the stale calibration comment made the false hang diagnosis more likely.

### Measured evidence

The last fully green run of this job was run `33137402410`, job `98740362395` (2026-08-28). Its pytest step ran `03:16:01Z -> 05:00:17Z` and ended:

```
74 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed, 79 warnings in 6252.74s (1:44:12)
```

That step's ~1,688 log lines carried one timestamp, `05:00:16`, because `pytest -q` writes newline-less progress dots and GitHub Actions timestamps a line only after it receives a newline.

### Root cause

`-q` was the buffering mechanism. `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` did not change the behavior, while `-v` streamed one line per completed test. Existing `-rA` and `--durations=25` are end-of-run reporters, and `--timeout=900 --timeout-method=thread` bounds one test rather than making multi-test progress visible.

## Scope and design

Only the `jira-dc-harness` lane is long enough for this silence to be operationally dangerous. The fix changes that lane from `-q` to `-v`, keeps its other pytest options, and corrects the calibration comment to the measured run id, duration, test count, and mean. Other lanes keep their existing verbosity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The `jira-dc-harness` pytest step in `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` uses `-v` rather than `-q`. Evidence: `origin/main:.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` runs `pytest -m external tests/external/live_jira_dc -v -rA --durations=25`, and the merged diff from `254d076c` changes only that lane from `-q`.
- [x] That step still passes `-rA`, `--durations=25`, `--timeout=900`, `--timeout-method=thread`, `-p no:cacheprovider`, and `--basetemp`. Evidence: the same `origin/main` run block retains all 6 options on the `jira-dc-harness` command.
- [x] The step's calibration comment states the measured green duration `6252.74s` rather than the stale `2384-2635s`. Evidence: the current comment cites `6252.74s`, while the parent of `254d076c` contained `2384-2635s`.
- [x] The step's calibration comment states the measured test count `76` rather than the stale `63`. Evidence: the current comment says the step ran over `76 tests`, while the parent of `254d076c` said `63 tests`.
- [x] The step's calibration comment cites the run id the measurement came from. Evidence: the current comment cites run `33137402410`, job `98740362395`, dated `2026-08-28`.
- [x] No other pytest invocation in `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` changes its `-q`/`-v` flag. Evidence: comparing the parent of `254d076c` with `origin/main` shows the cloud S3 and cloud mutation invocations still use `-q`; only the DC lane uses `-v`.
- [x] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` passes (exit 0) with no unadmitted new or increased entry. Evidence: the command passed in the detached `origin/main` worktree with `new=26 increased=0`, and every new entry was reported as `admitted`.
- [x] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports no new and no increased entries. Evidence: the command passed in the detached `origin/main` worktree with `new=0 increased=0`.
- [x] `make verify` is green apart from the known macOS-arm64 pandoc failures. Evidence: Gerrit Verified Gate run `35526291659` for change `3008` patchset 3 completed `success`, including lint/type-check and the CI gating pytest matrix for rev `18e04009738a`.
- [x] [non-codebase] A dispatched post-merge `external-integration.yml` run shows the DC harness pytest step emitting more than one distinct log timestamp.
  provenance: environment=GitHub Actions hosted runner running `external-integration.yml` run `35534905486` on `main` at `ba87827`; principal=the GitHub Actions workflow identity for the `jira DC harness smoke (real Jira Data Center, ephemeral)` job; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the criterion asks what a real dispatched run's log stream looks like, so the only admissible evidence is that run's own step log, which cannot be read from this repository's tree.

file_impact.reason: Change the jira-dc-harness pytest step from -q to -v so per-test progress streams, and correct the stale calibration comment to the measured green figures.
